entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

candidates.rationale: AI research/model company with frontier training infrastructure, similar market and buyer personas to OpenAI.

entity.name: Rhatigan Labs
entity.description:
Rhatigan Labs is an independent research and development practice building cognitive architecture for persistent AI systems.

Our work centers on the Wisdom Layer — an architecture that wraps around any language model to give it three-tier progressive memory, autonomous reflection cycles, self-criticism, and a behavioral-rule lifecycle. The goal: AI systems that genuinely develop over time rather than restart from zero every session.

The architecture has been extracted from 6+ months of continuous operation across three domains:
• Persistent agent research — 7 independent agents running continuously, producing documented autonomous epistemic self-correction on commodity-priced models.
• AI-assisted development — loom-code, a production coding utility deployed across 20+ repositories that accumulates interaction memory and distills it into targeted behavioral directives per codebase.
• Computational research — the same architecture applied to pharmacogenomics, producing 10,000+ cross-platform validated candidate associations across public datasets, with active academic collaboration discussions underway.

Our offerings:
• Wisdom Layer SDK — early-access Python SDK for persistent AI agents. Details at wisdomlayer.ai.
• Advisory & fractional CTO — for AI-native companies building long-horizon agent systems.
• Architect-in-Residence — ongoing strategic engagement for teams making foundational architectural decisions in agentic AI.

Founded and led by Jeff Rhatigan, drawing on 12+ years of enterprise architecture at Fortinet and TIBCO plus 9+ months of dedicated R&D on persistent cognitive systems.

entity.name: FRACTAL NEURONS
entity.description:
Fractal Neurons is an AI research system for pharma/biotech built around a private Dedicated Research Instance (DRI) deployed on-prem/VPC. It connects your internal R&D knowledge (reports, protocols, results, presentations) with external sources (literature, biological databases, patents) — but the key is how it retrieves and reasons.

We use shape-based retrieval: instead of hunting for the “right keyword,” researchers search by mechanism, structure, and causal logic. The system can match ideas even when the language is completely different (different terminology, discipline, or phrasing), and surface cross-domain analogies that would normally stay hidden in silos.

What this enables in practice:
	•	Identify pathways, targets, and mechanisms linked to a phenotype — even across inconsistent vocabularies
	•	Find experiments/models that actually discriminate between competing hypotheses
	•	Track what was tried before, under which conditions, and what failed (and why)
	•	Pull useful analogies from adjacent fields (another disease, tissue, modality, platform) to propose new directions

Unlike “pretty answers” from a generic chat interface, every output in Fractal Neurons comes with an evidence chain: sources, assumptions, and the full discovery path — making the reasoning reproducible, deterministic, and auditable. This matters in real R&D where decisions need to be defensible, not vibes-based.

Most LLM workflows create one-off insights that vanish after the conversation. Fractal Neurons builds an accumulative knowledge layer over time: what worked, what didn’t, and what would be required to reproduce or falsify a claim.

In short: we’re turning scientific discovery from a manual, memory-reliant process into an AI-native, traceable discovery pipeline — private, secure, and fully under the control of the research team.

candidates.rationale: Different niche: pharma/biotech research system, not a general AI platform like OpenAI; narrower use case and customer base.

entity.name: Admissible AI
entity.description:
Admissible AI provides runtime authority for AI decision commits.

As AI systems move from generating answers to taking actions, the core problem changes. When models use tools, write data, execute workflows, generate reports, approve actions, or update records, the question is no longer only whether an action is permitted.

The question is:

Is this decision admissible to commit?

Admissible AI sits between model output and durable consequence. The runtime evaluates proposed actions and decisions before they become real state, treating model output as a proposal rather than authority.

The runtime evaluates evidence sufficiency, uncertainty, contradiction, authority, scope, operating risk, rollback availability, and durable commit eligibility.

This is the distinction between governance and admissibility:

Governance asks whether an action is allowed.
Admissibility asks whether a decision is justified enough to become durable state.

Many high-risk AI failures will not come from obviously unauthorized behavior. They will come from systems that had permission, acted within policy, and still committed an invalid decision.

Admissible AI prevents that failure mode by enforcing a commit boundary around AI-generated decisions.

The runtime supports unregulated, policy-governed, and admissibility-governed comparison modes while keeping the underlying model constant. This makes the difference visible: fewer premature commits, clearer contradiction handling, stronger audit and replay, and safer durable state transitions.

Admissible AI is infrastructure for moving AI-generated decisions from proposal to action to persistent state without allowing invalid decisions to become real.

The goal is simple:

Make AI decisions admissible before they commit.

candidates.rationale: Different product category: OpenAI builds foundation models and apps; Admissible AI is governance/runtime control software for AI actions.
